name: Bastion
highlights: Next.js 16.1.6 → 16.2.12, which closes 28 published advisories. Two of them are the reason this is a release rather than a chore: a Middleware / Proxy bypass in App Router applications, and server-side request forgery through Server Actions and rewrites. This engine puts real properties in middleware — the CSP that decides who may frame a site, and on the control-plane side an auth gate that must fail closed and a host rewrite that must be unconditional — so a bypass class of bug is not theoretical here. Verified after upgrading: the frame-ancestors header still ships, and the control plane is still unreachable from the public hosts.

next-intl 4.8.3 → 4.13.4, closing an open redirect and a prototype pollution. The declared range already allowed the fix; only the lockfile was behind, which is the quiet way a patched advisory stays unpatched.

postcss and sharp are pinned by override. Next bundles its own copies (postcss 8.4.31, sharp 0.34.5) beneath the versions it resolves at the top level, so upgrading the direct dependency left the vulnerable copy in place — the tree had postcss twice, one patched and one not. Both are now single, patched copies in the engine and in Studio.

ESLint was walking generated build output. A bare `.next/**` ignore anchors at the repo root in flat config, so a nested `.next` was linted: ~9000 problems from 153 generated files, burying the ~40 real ones. The ignores are `**/`-prefixed now. This surfaces nine pre-existing react-hooks errors in engine components that nothing had been reporting, because `next build` on Turbopack does not run ESLint.

2.6.0: Four more modules stop being the reference build. Enabling label, merch, press or influence used to give a client somebody else's brand — his record label's name, website and four social accounts; his merch photos; his press bio, fact sheet and logo downloads; his Instagram feed and thirty-one partner logos. All of it is content now (roster.json gains a label object; merch.json, press.json and influencer.json are new), and every section renders only when this site has something to put in it.

Two payment and account bugs, both the same shape. /api/checkout hardcoded the reference build's hub product key, so a client whose membership.ts named their own product still resolved prices from another site's PriceTable — a real payment for the wrong thing. /api/account/profile did it for the hub's per-product store, reading and writing one site's visitor profiles under another site's key. Both now read the client's own key and refuse to run without it.

The structured data a client publishes is theirs. The MusicGroup listed four albums and three tracks as literals and the label Organization was written out in full, so search engines were told a client's site was about another artist's discography and another company's record label. Both are built from content, and both are omitted entirely when there is nothing to describe — a wrong machine-readable claim is worse than none.

Module pages read their photographs from content. Five hero images, the AI portrait, the tour posters, the links avatar and the merch previews all pointed into a public/ path that only exists in the reference build's repo, so a client enabling a module got a 404 where the page's first impression should be.

src/data/instagram.ts is no longer 404 lines of one person's feed. It survived the 2.5.0 sweep because the music page imports it too, which made it look structural; the posts are content and the file is now just the selectors.

The engine ships no client's name. A whole-tree audit of engine-owned files went from 46 files and 180 lines naming another build to zero — including the release codename, which had been a client's actual first name.
2.5.0: The last per-site data left engine code. src/data/artist.ts was a 500-line TypeScript literal holding one artist's discography, government roles, brand partnerships and academic CV — part of the FRAMEWORK, so any client running the music/ai/links/influencer modules inherited someone else's career. It is content now (artist.json + a validated loader), and 174 of those lines turned out to be exports nothing imported at all.

Enabling a module later no longer breaks the build. A module's loader is engine code that imports client-owned JSON, so switching a module on used to add the loader and nothing else. The sync now seeds the missing starter content in the same commit — from the TEMPLATE, not from this release, because the engine repo doubles as the reference build and its content is one particular site's.

The music/ai/influencer pages tolerate absent data: a track with no album, an experience entry with no logo, a skill with an unknown icon. They previously assumed every field the reference build happened to fill in.
2.4.1: Our own documents stop shipping to clients. CLAUDE.md (this framework plus fleet-wide operational context) and PRODUCTIZATION.md (the business model and price list) were seeded into every client repo by the template. An internal pricing document in a customer repository should not be possible; both are excluded now.
2.4.0: The default home page is content, not code. It hardcoded the reference build's headline numbers, partner logos, three role panels, a featured post and a latest release — so every client shipped a home page advertising another artist, behind links to modules they had switched off and image paths that 404 in a client repo. It now reads src/data/home.json and skips whatever is absent; {} is a valid home, which is the right shape for a site that composes its own with the pages module.
Role panels only render when the module they link into is enabled. Three panels pointing at 404s was the previous behaviour on every client build.

The MusicGroup and label Organization schemas moved out of the root layout onto their own modules' pages. Emitting them sitewide claimed every page was about a music group, and it pinned one artist's discography into a core file that shipped to every client.
The label roster is content (src/data/roster.json + a validated loader), so one label's artists are no longer part of the engine.

src/config/membership.ts is client-owned. It is documented as a per-client file but was classified engine, so every client inherited a membership gate pointed at the reference build's product on the accounts hub — and src/lib/membership.ts no longer falls back to that product key, because a wrong-but-plausible answer from the hub is worse than failing closed.
2.3.1: The reference build's personal artefacts (Wikipedia draft, Wikidata sync scripts) moved to scripts/private/ and are now EXCLUDED from the sync. They were 57 mentions of another person's name in every client repo, engine-adjacent only by accident of living under scripts/.
The remaining build scripts no longer hardcode the reference build in default paths, logo filenames or DOM selectors.
2.3.0: A client repo now only carries code for the modules it enables. requireModule() already 404s a disabled module's routes, which is enough for a visitor and nothing else: the FILES still shipped, so every client repo contained the reference build's music pages, its record-label roster, its Instagram data and its press quotes — dead weight in their build and another brand's copy in their repo. The sync no longer offers a disabled module's files, and offers the ones already present for removal.

Ownership is derived, not hand-listed: requireModule() calls give the gated subtree, imports are followed forward, and a file is prunable only when EVERY module that can reach it is disabled and no core entrypoint reaches it. Generated into packages/schema/src/module-paths.ts by `npm run module-paths`; a file the table doesn't know about is never pruned.

Measured on the first real client (crm + pages + posts): 70 files removed and the build goes from 351 prerendered pages to 45. Reversible — turning a module back on makes the next sync restore its files.
2.2.1: The light hero wash no longer erases the subject on a phone. Its top band was 72% paper over 190px — doing the navbar's job over exactly the 120–180px where a head lands on a narrow frame — so a hero cropped to show a face showed a rumour of one. Now 58% over 120px, which still carries dark ink over a bright plate.
2.2.0: Mobile is tighter. The band-padding FLOOR governs every viewport up to ~933px, so a floor of 3.5rem meant every section on a phone was separated by 112px of nothing; the hero is shorter and its bottom padding smaller now that the fact row is hidden. Desktop is bit-identical — above 933px the vw term wins either way.

The web app manifest is generated from config (src/app/manifest.ts) instead of being a static file copied into every client's public/. It was never replaced after copying, so the first real client's live site offered to install as an app named after the reference build, with a music-producer description, on their own domain.

favicon.ico moved out of src/app/ (engine-owned) into public/ (client-owned). Next serves the app-dir icon with precedence, so the sync had been shipping the reference build's favicon into every client repo and overriding theirs — verified by md5: the first client's live favicon was byte-identical to ours.

Fourteen route layouts stopped hardcoding the reference build's domain in their canonical + hreflang tags. A canonical is an instruction to index the OTHER url, so this was pointing clients' SEO at somebody else's site; the language map was also fixed at five locales, advertising alternates that 404 for an en-only build. Both now come from site.url and site.locales via routeAlternates().
The schema.org graph no longer carries hardcoded reference-build URLs in @id, url and publisher fields.
2.1.3: schema.org `nationality` now emits a country. `location.from` is written for humans ("Mwenezi, Zimbabwe"), and the whole string was being published as a Country name — so the structured data search engines read declared a Country named after a rural district.

Core-route photo heroes (contact, about) now follow the theme instead of forcing a dark band onto a light page. A light-theme site was opening its contact page on a near-black slab with a light-ink navbar over it — the same defect composed-page heroes had before they gained a light plate, on the routes nobody re-checked. Name a bright frame in Brand → "Page hero photo — light mode".

The light hero wash is rebalanced. At 97% paper it was legible but the photograph was gone; it now sits at a tested middle where the image reads as colour and place and dark ink keeps a comfortable margin. All four scrims (light/dark × wide/narrow) live in one shared module, because these numbers had already been wrong twice in two components.

A hero's fact row (Based in / Field / Affiliation) is hidden below the sm breakpoint. On a phone it became ~200px of stacked label/value pairs that pushed the affiliations marquee — the thing that establishes credibility at a glance — entirely below the fold. Still in the DOM for crawlers and screen readers, still on desktop.
Pillar cards take an optional photograph, so the set where a reader decides which domain is theirs isn't three blocks of text.

The footer credits the build ("A Tzohar site — built by Ebenworks & Statotech") and no longer prints the subject's birthplace as if it were an address; that fact still feeds the about page and the schema.org Person.
2.1.1: Light-mode heroes were unreadable on a phone: the narrow white wash mirrored the dark ramp's opacities, and the mobile crop was shared between two different photographs, putting a face directly behind the title.
New positionMobileLight so a light plate can be cropped for narrow screens on its own.
Studio can edit the whole background — the light-mode photo, its scrim and both crops.
2.1.0: Studio's preview is now this site itself, framed and fed your unsaved draft — same components, CSS, fonts and motion as production, because it is production rendering a draft. It replaced a miniature re-implementation that rendered 9 sections where a real page had 12.
Appearance changes (colour, font, paper, radius, mode) apply live with no reload, using the same CSS generator the server injects — so they look right rather than approximately right.
Selecting a section in Studio scrolls this site's preview to it and flashes it.
Real device viewports — 1440 / 1280 / 834 / 390 with rotate — sized in true CSS pixels so this site's own media queries decide the layout.
2.0.0: Five new page-section types: gallery (lightbox), video (poster + inline player), journey (annotated map/timeline), portfolio (printable one-pager), postList (filterable article index).
Posts — a dated, reverse-chronological writing surface with categories, drafts and a safe plain-text body, separate from composed pages.
A client-facing CMS at /admin: posts, page sections, media uploads and site settings, committed straight to the repo. No hub account, no dependency on Studio being up.
Heroes gained a light-mode plate, per-mode scrims and a mobile crop, so one hero block can be dark-cinematic and light-airy without duplicating it.
Navigation panels with icons, blurbs and a feature tile; card grids gained an index variant for small source images.
Every route's SEO, every transactional email and the schema.org Person now read from site config instead of carrying the previous client's copy.
Contact inquiry forms are chosen in config, and filtered to the ones this build has copy for, so a trimmed messages file can never break the page.
Contrast-corrected paper palettes — the noir preset's tonal ladder is separable in both modes, and ink-3 clears 4.6:1 on every band tone.
